children: Baker Hughes reported a lower profit but growing revenue boosted by an increase in demand across a range of energy and industrial markets.
The energy company on Tuesday reported a third-quarter profit of $411 million, or 41 cents a share, compared with a profit of $609 million, or 61 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings were 70 cents a share. Analysts surveyed by FactSet were expecting 61 cents a share.
Revenue rose 14% to $8.03 billion. Analysts were expecting $7.75 billion.

In the industrial and energy technology unit, sales rose 3% year over year to $3.48 billion. The oilfield services and equipment business had sales tick up 1% to $3.66 billion. Chart Industries, a thermal management company Baker Hughes acquired this summer, brought in $888 million in revenue during the quarter.
Baker Hughes also reported $10.76 billion in orders during the quarter, up 31% year over year.
The company raised its outlook for orders in its industrial and energy technology segment between 2026 and 2028 to upwards of $50 billion.

"Energy security, rising demand for AI and emerging opportunities across growth markets are creating new opportunities across our energy upstream, energy infrastructure and industrial end markets," Chief Executive Lorenzo Simonelli said.
